**Test image**: Green banana fingers (pods) on a bunch, with dark brown/black discoloration concentrated at the distal (flower/tip) ends of multiple fruits. The affected tissue appears shrunken and blackened at the tips while the rest of the fruit remains green.

**Comparison summary**:
- **Cigar_End_Rot** (PlantWild_30, PlantWild_59): Near-perfect match — green banana pods with dark black rot specifically at the tips/cigar ends, same presentation as test image
- **Anthracnose** (PlantWild_26, PlantWild_32): Scattered sunken black lesions all over ripe/yellow banana skin — completely different pattern from the test image
- **All leaf classes** (Banana_Bunchy_Top_Virus, Bunchy_Top, Cordana_Leaf_Spot, Panama_Disease, Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka): All show leaf symptoms — not relevant to the pod/fruit shown in the test image

The blackening specifically at the distal tip of each finger, while the fruit is still green and on the plant, is the hallmark signature of **Cigar End Rot** — infection spreading from the perianth (flower remnant) inward.
